answer.rationale: P99 latency at 5x target on write path coincides with release 2 hours ago during settlement peak. Memory_b6 shows staged release gating caught regressions rapidly; memory_b1 demonstrates rollback of a problematic build cleared errors without customer impact. The timing correlation (release → degradation) is strong. Rollback is the highest-confidence intervention because: (1) it directly addresses the likely root cause, (2) it's fast and reversible, (3) settlement writes must succeed—rollback protects write availability better than capacity adds or routing changes would during peak load. Circuit breakers and read replicas don't address write path latency. Regional failover adds complexity when the problem is likely local to the release. One intervention capacity means rollback now prevents cascading failure during peak settlement traffic.
